title: Existence of the open and topos part of the admissible presentation
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair, I finitely generated, and U the open complement of V(I). There exists a small site (C,τ), with C in universe u+1, an AdmissibleToposPresentation I C τ as defined in [def-per-admissible-modification-presentation-data], and AdmissibleOpenEmbeddings I U as defined in [def-per-admissible-modification-coefficient-data]. Thus the actual full-support modification category is thin and cofiltered, the indicated site presents its closed-fibre topos limit with conservative compatible geometric points, and the cartesian common-open embeddings are natural in domination. No completed site, coefficient colimit, cohomology, or spectral sequence is part of this conclusion.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373: admissible blowups, (**) and its limit; p.374 final Note for the formal closed-fibre identification.

proof.text: Use the filtered domination preorder and the schematically dense open immersions supplied by [lem-per-admissible-modification-system]. Between two of these blowups there is at most one $X$-morphism: two $X$-morphisms $B_K\to B_J$ both restrict to the identity of $U$, $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $B_K$, and $B_J\to X$ is separated (it is proper), so they are equal by [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated]. Hence the transition morphisms are unique and compose correctly. Quotient by isomorphism of blowups to get a small cofiltered index category (ideals of the fixed ring form a set). The properness theorem [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper] applies because each $J$ is finitely generated. The closed fibres are proper over the affine $Z$ by [lem-kun-proper-stability], hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. The transition morphisms are qcqs: by [lem-sfb-closed-graph-universally-closed-diagram] their graphs into $B_K\times_XB_J$ are closed since $B_J/X$ is separated, the graphs are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and projection to $B_J$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. Restricting to the closed fibres gives a cofiltered diagram of qcqs schemes. These observations verify the geometric hypotheses of the limit-site construction, without an excellence assumption. The common-open embeddings are the inverses of the blowup isomorphisms over U; they are cartesian, and uniqueness on the common open gives their naturality.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, finite-stage (**) and its limit; final Note.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-qcqs-etale-topos-inverse-limit] to $(Z_J)$. Its finite-cover colimit site presents $\mathcal T$, the projections are the $p_J$, and its conservative points are compatible geometric points of the closed fibres. The terminal object is represented by every $Z_J$. Hence the global-section version of finite-cover continuity applies, rather than a theorem about inverse limits of schemes with affine transition maps. Express the projection functors as continuous functors from the full small etale categories. Their canonical pushforward comparisons satisfy the cocycle with every coefficient category. This yields AdmissibleToposPresentation together with AdmissibleOpenEmbeddings, with no spectral-sequence or completion assertion.
